title: Harden TensorRT-RTX runtime-cache compatibility, observability and benchmark semantics
decisions: TensorRT-RTX runtime-cache reuse requires an explicit cache identity containing GPU SKU, TensorRT-RTX version, CUDA-context Compute-in-Graphics state and cache-origin NVIDIA driver version.

A runtime cache is compatible only when GPU SKU is equivalent, TensorRT-RTX version matches exactly, CiG state matches exactly and the runtime driver is greater than or equal to the cache-origin driver.

An incompatible TensorRT-RTX runtime cache may be ignored by upstream and trigger transparent JIT kernel recompilation without an application error; FA3 therefore requires cache-hit/cache-miss/JIT-rebuild observability evidence.
First-inference JIT compilation cost must be separated from steady-state cached inference benchmarks and cannot be silently reported as a cache-hit result.
TensorRT-RTX timing-cache APIs are deprecated upstream and have no effect on the built TensorRT-RTX engine; they are not the FA3 canonical runtime-cache path for new integrations.
Runtime caches remain derived, disposable and noncanonical artifacts; cache incompatibility invalidates reuse, not source-model identity.
